text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--- Denmark's Confederation of Industry wants to scotch the fall in the number of new production companies being set up by introducing tax reliefs or rescheduling dates for paying tax.

--- Sales of organically produced milk have doubled in 1996, accounting for some 10 percent of total milk sales in Denmark at 130 million kilos per year, the vast bulk of it produced by leading dairies MD Foods and Kloever Milk.
--- In a letter to retail chains and associations Denmark's National Consumer Council warns against violating credit rules by advertising interest-free credit schemes on consumer goods.

--- Danish AIDS experts are enthusiastic about a new enzyme HIV-inhibiting treatment introduced six months ago. A survey of 3,000 patients in 20 countries including Denmark, shows that the treatment can reduce death rates among AIDS patients by one third during a period of two years.

--- Economy minister Marianne Jelved warns that Denmark will become politically isolated in the European Union along with Britain, Greece and Sweden if it continues to opt out of participation in the common European currency (EMU).
--- Foreign investors on the Danish share market complain that inadequate information on the identity of shareholders in Danish companies is keeping overseas investors from investing in Denmark.
